verses.1: These rapid Soma-drops have been poured through the purifying sieve. To bring us all felicities.
verses.2: Dispelling manifold mishap, giving the courser's progeny, Yea, and the warrior steed's, success.
verses.3: Bringing prosperity to kine, they pour perpetual strengthening food On us for noble eulogy.
verses.4: King Pavamana is implored with holy songs, on man's behalf, To travel through, the realm of air.
verses.5: Pressed for the banquet of the Gods, O Soma, bring us might,and speed, Like beauty for a'brilliant show!
verses.6: Bring us, O Indu, hundredfold increase of kine, and noble steeds. The gift of fortune for our help!
verses.7: With sacrifice we seek to thee fair cherisher of manly might In mansons of the lofty heavens.
verses.8: Drink gladdening, crusher of the bold, praiseworthy, with most mighty sway, Destroyer of a hundred forts.
verses.9: Hence riches came to thee, the King, O sapient one: the strong-winged bird, Unwearied, brought thee from the sky.
verses.10: And now, sent forth, he hath attained to mighty power and majesty, Active and ready to assist.
verses.11: That each may see the light, the bird brought us the guard of Law, the friend O fall, the speeder through the air.
verses.12: For food, flow onward with thy stream, cleansed and made bright by sapient men: Indu, with sheen approach the milk!
verses.13: While thou art cleansed, song-lover. bring comfort and vigourto the folk, Poured, tawny one! on milk and curds!
verses.14: Purified for feast of Gods, go thou to Indra's resting-place, Resplendent, furthered by the strong!
verses.15: By Agni Agni is inflamed, Lord of the house, wise, young,. who bears Our gifts: the ladle is his mouth.
verses.16: God, Agni, be his sure defence who, lord of sacrificial gifts. Worshippeth thee the messenger.
verses.17: Be gracious, brilliant Godl to him who, rich in sacred gifts,would fain Call Agni to the feast of Gods!
verses.18: Mitra of holy strength I call, and foe-destroying Varuna, Who perfect prayer with offered oil.
verses.19: By Law, O Mitra, Varuna, Law-strengtheners who cleave to Law, Have ye obtained your lofty power.
verses.20: The Sages, Mitra, Varuna, of wide dominion, mighty ones, Bestow on us effectual strength.
verses.21: So mayst thou verily be seen coming with fearless Indra: both Of equal splendour, bringing bliss!
verses.22: Thereafter they, as is their wont, resumed the state of new-born babes, Taking their sacrificial name.
verses.23: Thou, Indra, with the rapid Gods who shatter even what is firm, Even in the cave didst find the cows.
verses.24: I call the twain whose deed wrought here hath all been famed in ancient time: Indra and Agni harm us not!
verses.25: The strong, the scatterers of the foe, Indra and Agni we invoke: May they be kind to one like me:
verses.26: Ye slay our Arya foes, O Lords of heroes, slay our Dasa foes: Ye drive all enemies away.
verses.27: The living drops of Soma juice pour, as they flow the gladdening drink, Intelligent drops above the station of the sea, exhilarating, dropping meath.
verses.28: May Pavamana, King and God, speed with his wave over the sea the lofty rite! Do thou by Mitra's and by Varuna's decree flow furthering the lofty rite:
verses.29: Far-seeing, lovely, guided by the men, the God whose habitation is the sea!
verses.30: Three are the voices that the car-steed utters: he speaks the lore of prayer, the thought of Order. To the cows' master come the cows inquiring: the hymns with eager longing come to Soma.
verses.31: To Soma come the cows, the milch-kine longing, to Soma sages with their hymns inquiring. Soma, effused, is purified and lauded: our hymns and Trishtup songs unite in Soma.
verses.32: Thus, Soma, as we pour thee into vessels, while thou art purified, flow for our welfare! Pass into Indra. with great joy and rapture: make the voice swell, and generate abundance!
verses.33: O Indra, if a hundred heavens and if a hundred earths were thine,-- No, not a hundred suns could match thee at thy birth, not both the worlds, O Thunderer.
verses.34: Thou, hero, hast performed thy hero deeds with might, yea, all with strength, O strongest one. Maghavan, help us to a stable full of kine, O Thunderer, with wondrous aids!
verses.35: We compass thee like water, we whose grass is trimmed and Soma pressed. Here where the filter pours its stream, thy worshippers round thee, O Vritra-slayer, sit.
verses.36: Men, Vasu! by the Soma with lauds call thee to the foremost place. When cometh he athirst unto the juice as home, O Indra, like a bellowing bull?
verses.37: O valiant hero, boldly win thousandfold spoil with Kanva's sons! O active Maghavan, with eager prayer we crave the yellowhued with store of kine.
verses.38: With Plenty for his true ally the active man will gain the spoil. Your Indra, much-invoked, I bend with song, as bends a wright his wheel of solid wood.
verses.39: They who bestow great riches love not paltry praise: wealth comes not to the niggard churl. Light is the task to give, O Maghavan, to one like me on the decisive day.
verses.40: Three several words are uttered: kine are lowing cows. who give the milk: The tawny-hued goes bellowing on.
verses.41: The young and sacred mothers of the holy rite have uttered praise, Embellishing the Child of Heaven.
verses.42: From every side, O Soma, for our profit, pour thou forth four seas. Filled full of riches thousandfold!
verses.43: The Somas, very rich in sweets, for which the sieve is distined, flow Effused, the source of Indra's joy: may you strong juices reach the Gods!
verses.44: Indu flows on for Indra's sake,-thus have the deities declared. The Lord of Speech exerts himself, controller of all power and might.
verses.45: Inciter of the voice of song, with thousand streams the ocean flows. Even Soma, Lord of opulence, the friend of Indra, day by day.
verses.46: SPREAD is thy cleansing filter, Brahmanaspati: as prince thou enterest its limbs from every side. The raw; whose mass bath not been heated. gains not this: they only which are dressed, which bear, attain to it.
verses.47: High in the seat of heaven is placed the scorcher's sieve: its, threads are standing separate, glittering with light. The swift ones favour him who purifieth this: with brilliancy they mount up to the height of heaven.
verses.48: The foremost spotted Steer bath made the Mornings shine: he bellows, fain for war, among created things. By his high wisdom have the mighty Sages wrought: the Fathers who behold mankind laid down the germ.
verses.49: Sing forth to him, the holy, most munificent, sublime with his refulgent glow, To Agni, ye Upastutas
verses.50: Worshipped with gifts, enkindled, splendid, Maghavan shall win himself heroic fame: And will not his more plentiful benevolence come to us with abundant strength?
verses.51: We sing this strong and wild delight of thine which conquers in the fray, Which, Caster of the Stone! gives room and shines like gold.
verses.52: Wherewith thou foundest shining lights for Ayu and for Manu's sake: Now joying in this sacred grass thou bearnest forth.
verses.53: This day too singers of the hymn praise, as of old, this might of thine: Win thou the waters every day, thralls of the strong!
verses.54: O Indra, hear Tirschi's call, the call of him who serveth thee. Satisfy him with wealth of kine and valient offspring! Great art thou.
verses.55: For he, O Indra, hath produced for thee the newest gladdening song, A hymn that springs from careful drop thought, ancient and full of sacred truth.
verses.56: That Indra will we laud whom songs and hymns of praise have magnified. Striving to win, we celebrate his many deeds of hero might.
